tools.name: build_handoff
tools.description:
Build one product's reference as a complete prompt: ordered screens with notes, observed
transitions, links to up to 10 agent-sized images (1x copies and section crops, each with its
pixel size), the measured design guide and an implementation checklist; the same prompt as
the site's "Use in agent"

tools.name: build_recipe
tools.description:
The best way to build from references, with or without a person: pass 2 to 6 screen ids from
search_screens (each "id: what to take from it") and get one Markdown brief with the
screenshots attached at 1x (section crops for long pages), measured component sizes, the
page structure and what to take f

tools.name: check_my_ui
tools.description:
Compare the user's UI structure with the closest real products. Describe what they have
(screen type, sections, flow steps, plan count; no personal names, prices or customer data)
and get factual comparisons, not recommendations: plan counts, section order, blocks the
references have that theirs lac

tools.name: compare_pricing
tools.description:
A fact table of 2 to 8 captured pricing pages, for research rather than building: per product,
plan names and prices, cheapest paid plan with currency, monthly/yearly toggle and saving, free
plan, trial, seat model, enterprise tier, notable limits, captured date and page url, plus a
Markdown table.

tools.name: compare_screens
tools.description:
Compare two screens side by side (screen types, page sections, observed actions, dimensions,
plan counts), e.g. Linear's pricing page with Stripe's, or one screen against a description
of what the user is building (targetDescription).

tools.name: find_related_screens
tools.description:
Find screens from other products that solve the same design problem as this one: same primary
pattern first, then shared tasks, states and components (rarer tags count more). At most two per
product; each says why it matched, and a dark-theme copy folds into its row as variants. Use it after one goo

tools.name: get_design
tools.description:
Get a product's measured design guide: fonts, colour palette, type scale, layout and
component observations, measured separately for its marketing site and product UI. Use it
for "make it look like <product>" or "trustworthy like <product>": take the tokens from here
and the structure from its scree

tools.name: get_email_flow
tools.description:
One company's onboarding emails in order: strategy, takeaways, and each email's day, stage,
sender, subject, preheader and buttons. detail=full adds text; images=N attaches N emails.

tools.name: get_flow
tools.description:
Get a product's captured flow: every step in order with title, notes, page url, observed
transitions (button labels and where they lead) and which steps are alternate branches, plus
the handoffId for build_handoff. Use it to study how a product structures signup, onboarding
or a task; then get_scree

tools.name: get_motion
tools.description:
Get one motion entry as a build prompt: what moves and how (every property, duration, easing
or spring, delay and trigger), why it feels good, how to adapt it to another size, the
accessibility it needs, Screenrove's vanilla HTML/CSS/JS and the original source where its
license allows. Values are ma

tools.name: get_motion_guidelines
tools.description:
House rules for UI motion (durations, enter and exit easing, springs, reduced motion) with
duration and easing tokens and the library's categories and triggers. Read it once before
adding animation.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description:
Get one product's collection: what was captured (coverageLabel, coverage, captureNote) and
every screen, grouped into flow, marketing and product, one line each (id, title, primary
pattern, page url). detail=full adds each screen's notes and tags. Use it to explore a
competitor's whole UI; then get_

tools.name: get_screen
tools.description:
Get everything recorded about one screen: notes on what it does and how it's laid out, product,
captured date, page url, source URL, dimensions, observed actions and where they lead, and page
sections for long marketing pages. The notes are not the screen: call get_screen_image with the
same id to s

tools.name: get_screen_image
tools.description:
See the screen; call it on your top picks before writing UI. preview (default) is 1x, so
1 image px = 1 CSS px (the top of a long page). The text gives its pixel size and a long
page's sections: section=N returns one as a 1x crop. size=full is the original (often 2x),
refused above 8000 px tall.

tools.name: list_email_flows
tools.description:
Real onboarding email sequences from 97 SaaS products (684 emails) after a fresh
signup: emails, days, week-one count and stages per flow. Then get_email_flow or search_emails.

tools.name: list_flows
tools.description:
List captured user journeys (signup and onboarding, checkout, booking, search, marketplace,
and task flows such as building a board) with step counts and flow type, 40 at a time. A
flowType marked typeInferred was read from the flow's first steps; flows with no type are
left out of a flowType filter

tools.name: list_products
tools.description:
List the 191 products in the catalog, one compact line each: id, name, category,
a one-line coverageLabel saying what was captured (signed in or logged out only), screen
counts and page url. Paged (50 by default) and filterable by category or q; the first page
also counts products per category. To f

tools.name: list_tags
tools.description:
List the tag vocabulary for searching by design problem: four facets (task, pattern, component,
state), each tag with its definition, aliases and how many screens carry it.

Use the ids with search_screens or pick_reference, e.g. pattern=board-view or state=empty.

tools.name: name_patterns
tools.description:
How real products are named: pattern shares with examples, TLDs, domain styles, length and
syllables, a per-category table and highlights such as the share of AI tools on .ai. Takes
search_names' filters for one slice. Use it before proposing names.

tools.name: pick_reference
tools.description:
Show a person 2 to 6 matching references side by side in their browser and let them click the
one to build from. Returns a URL to open for them; then call wait_for_pick with the pickId for
their choice and a build prompt. Only when a person is there to choose: autonomous agents
should use build_reci

tools.name: search_emails
tools.description:
One kind of onboarding email across companies, by words, stage, product and send day
(e.g. stage=trial-ended). Attaches the top result's image.

tools.name: search_logos
tools.description:
Logo references for designing a logo or app icon: each library product's own mark as its
site serves it (never redrawn) with mark type, colours, shape, letter case, brand font and
category, e.g. "lettermarks on a rounded tile", "green symbols". Logos are trademarks of their
owners: study them, don't

tools.name: search_motion
tools.description:
Search the motion library: UI animations and micro-interactions (button presses, toggles,
toasts, number tickers, check-offs, thinking states, hover effects, sounds) from open-source
libraries and designers' recordings, each with an exact spec and most with vanilla code. Any
word can match ("habit s

tools.name: search_names
tools.description:
Naming ideas grounded in about 700 real product names, each with domain, TLD, category, naming
pattern, length, syllables, casing and domain style (getX.com, Xhq.com…), plus stats for the
whole match, e.g. "short invented names for AI tools on .ai". Traits are heuristics; check
trademarks and domain

tools.name: search_screens
tools.description:
Find screens by design problem and keyword, e.g. "pricing page like Stripe", "settings",
"empty project list". Every screen is tagged on four facets: task, pattern (screen archetype),
component and state. Commas mean OR within a facet, facets combine with AND, e.g.
pattern=list-view,table-view and s

tools.name: suggest_polish
tools.description:
Given the parts of a UI (elements, a description, or Screenrove screen ids; from a screenshot,
list the parts you see), returns motion entries and sounds that would improve each part, plus
new touches it doesn't have yet (additions), not only replacements. Then get_motion each one.

tools.name: wait_for_pick
tools.description:
Wait for the person to choose on the pick page. Long-polls up to 50 seconds and returns as
soon as they click, or status "pending" (call again). Once chosen: their reference with its

findings.detail: Description of "search_names" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: build_recipe, get_email_flow, get_flow, get_motion, get_product, get_screen, list_email_flows, list_products, pick_reference, search_emails, search_screens · Private data: build_recipe, get_design, get_motion_guidelines · Public sink: get_email_flow, list_email_flows, name_patterns, search_emails.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: build_recipe, get_email_flow, get_flow, get_motion, get_product, get_screen, list_email_flows, list_products, pick_reference, search_emails, search_screens · Private data: build_recipe, get_design, get_motion_guidelines · Public sink: get_email_flow, list_email_flows, name_patterns, search_emails

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
